name: Witch Doctor: Spirit Striker raises the Serpent Ward's Voodoo Fire proc chance (#824)
contract: #824: Spirit Striker 806286 carries ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER (aura 107), EffectMiscValue 18 (SPELLMOD_CHANCE_OF_SUCCESS), EffectBasePoints 9 (real value 10), EffectSpellClassMask word1 bit 27 (134217728), matching exactly the SpellFamilyFlags[1] of Voodoo Fire One 802262 (ProcChance 20) and Voodoo Fire Two 803846 (ProcChance 40). The Serpent Ward's UpdateAI (AscensionWitchDoctorSummons.cpp) rolled that chance as a hardcoded C++ literal (20 or 40) via roll_chance_f, never through Player::ApplySpellMod, so the registered spellmod was silently dropped -- a real_bug (Spirit Striker's +10% had zero gameplay effect). The fix adds player->ApplySpellMod(VoodooFireOne/Two, SPELLMOD_CHANCE_OF_SUCCESS, chance) before the roll, matching the existing pattern in AscensionPrimalistJudgement.cpp/AscensionPyromancerEvents.cpp. spell_modifier on VoodooFireOne is NOT usable proof here: the aura is a plain core-generic ADD_FLAT_MODIFIER, so it registers on the player identically before and after the fix -- it only proves the aura loaded, not that the pet code consults it (this is the exact trap the investigation flagged). The gameplay-test harness also has no metric that can attribute a spell cast or spell-damage event to a player-owned TempSummon actor: spell_cast_count/spell_proc_count key off GetUnit(actor), which only resolves to a player (_actors) or a harness 'creatures' fixture (_targets), and spell_go_count/spell_damage_count/spell_damage_total require the actor to BE a player and restrict 'caster' to that player's own GUID or Player::GetPetGUID() (a formal pet); the Serpent Ward is summoned via Player::SummonCreature + SetOwnerGUID, never registered as a formal Pet or as a harness target, so none of those metrics can isolate its casts (confirmed by reading src/server/coa/CoAGameplayTest.cpp, not assumed). The only available proof is therefore statistical: the enemy fixture's own health loss, compared in the same run before vs after learning 806286, over ~140 Serpent Ward attack ticks per phase (WardAttackInterval=2000ms, no haste). Voodoo Fire (500473, EffectBasePoints 72, no per-level scaling) fires only on a successful roll; Serpent Ward Attack (573055, EffectBasePoints 4 + EffectRealPointsPerLevel 2.3 -> about 186 at level 80) fires every tick regardless, so it dominates the mean damage and dilutes the ratio signal: with p=0.2 to p=0.3 the expected ratio of phase-2-to-phase-1 health loss is only around 1.036 by this rough theoretical calculation (not measured on a live server); 1.02 is used as a deliberately conservative pass/fail line, closer to the unfixed side than the midpoint, so a false PASS on unfixed code is rarer than a false FAIL on fixed code. This statistical distinguisher was designed from DBC constants only (BasePoints, ProcChance, RealPointsPerLevel) and was NOT executed against a live worldserver (out of scope for this task, no build/deploy performed) at authoring time; it does not account for the Serpent Ward's own possible spell-crit chance or partial magic-resist rolls against the fixture, both unverified, so the true false-pass/false-fail rate could exceed the theoretical ~15% two-sided estimate documented in fix-824.md. It is included as the best available same-run, server-numbers regression signal given this constraint, not as a low-flake guarantee. Hex of Malice 501158 is cast once purely to put the caster in combat with the enemy fixture (Unit::SetInCombatWith on the original caster is required for AscensionWitchDoctor::Enemy() to ever hand the ward a target) and its own damage (instant hit + a 24000 ms DOT, SpellDuration.dbc row 106) is fully waited out before either measured phase begins, so it never contaminates the comparison. REPAIR NOTE (live-run corrections, see repair-witchdoctor-fix-spirit-striker-voodoo-fire-proc.md): (1) the original scenario cast Hex of Malice (501158) without a preceding `learn` step, so `HandleCastSpellOpcode` rejected it (`spell_active: false` in the recorded run) and combat/damage never started at all -- fixed by adding `learn` 501158 before the cast. (2) Serpent Ward's own summon spell 500960 carries `DurationIndex=3` -> SpellDuration.dbc row 3 `Duration=60000` (a hard 60 s TEMPSUMMON_TIMED_DESPAWN, confirmed by DBC read and by `Player::SummonCreature(entry, position, TEMPSUMMON_TIMED_DESPAWN, duration)` in `AscensionWitchDoctor::Summon`), far shorter than the original single 280000 ms wait per phase -- a live run showed the ward attacking for only its first ~30 ticks then sitting despawned for the rest of both phases (phase1 measured delta -2750, phase2 measured delta ~0). Fixed by periodically re-casting 500960 (every 56000 ms, safely under the 60000 ms despawn) throughout each phase: 500960 carries `SPELL_ATTR7_CAN_BE_MULTI_CAST` and `SPELL_ATTR2_DO_NOT_RESET_COMBAT_TIMERS` and 0 RecoveryTime/CategoryRecoveryTime (confirmed by DBC read), and `AscensionWitchDoctor::Summon` explicitly despawns the previous same-slot ward before spawning the new one, so recasting cleanly replaces the ward with a fresh 60 s instance without a cooldown block, a double-ward moment, or a combat-timer reset -- `owned_creature_count` stays at 1 throughout. (3) A live run with (1) and (2) fixed still produced a flat ratio (0.988, phase-1 delta -24687 over ~140 ticks, phase-2 delta slightly smaller) instead of the ~1.036 expected from a working fix. Read `802262` VoodooFireOne's own DBC record: `Effect[1]=6 SPELL_EFFECT_APPLY_AURA`/`EffectApplyAuraName[1]=4 SPELL_AURA_DUMMY` on `TARGET_UNIT_CASTER` -- casting/learning 802262 is what makes `player->HasAura(VoodooFireOne)` true, and the scenario never granted it. `AscensionWitchDoctorSummons.cpp`'s ward `UpdateAI` gates the entire proc mechanism on `player->HasAura(VoodooFireTwo) ? VoodooFireTwo : player->HasAura(VoodooFireOne) ? VoodooFireOne : 0` -- without either aura, `voodooFireRank` is always 0, `chance` is always 0, `roll_chance_f(chance)` never fires, and the fix's own `if (voodooFireRank) player->ApplySpellMod(...)` line is dead code for the whole run, in both phases equally -- exactly matching the observed flat ratio. (`802262`'s `Effect[0]=190 SPELL_EFFECT_ASCENSION_APPLY_AURA_TO_SUMMONS` with `EffectApplyAuraName[0]=42 SPELL_AURA_PROC_TRIGGER_SPELL`/`EffectTriggerSpell[0]=500473` looks like it could be an independent core-native proc path, but `Aura::GetProcEffectMask`, `src/server/game/Spells/Auras/SpellAuras.cpp:2156`, requires `sSpellMgr->GetSpellProcEntry(GetId())` to be non-null, i.e. a `spell_proc` SQL row, and `SpellMgr::LoadSpellProcs` loads only from that table with no DBC fallback -- confirmed no `spell_proc` row exists for 802262/803846, so this path is dead and the hardcoded `UpdateAI` roll is confirmed as the sole live mechanism, consistent with fix-824.md.) Fixed by adding `learn` 802262 (VoodooFireOne, the tier matching the scenario's existing `spell_modifier` base-20 asserts) right after learning 500960. This third fix was applied after the task's 3-run budget was exhausted and is therefore UNVERIFIED by an actual green run -- see repair-witchdoctor-fix-spirit-striker-voodoo-fire-proc.md for the full evidence chain and the explicit unresolved/needs-one-more-run status.

Let the ward settle before entering combat
Hex of Malice puts the caster in combat with the fixture
